title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
gist: House House disclosed that LLMs helped fix a Unity shadow bug in Big Walk (under 0.1% of code), igniting an IGF jury revolt in which 19 jurors pledged not to vote for any game using generative AI. The fight exposes a split between zero-tolerance purists and those who say disclosure is being punished, with Valve's narrower disclosure rules as a key policy contrast.

insights.claim: Nineteen members of the 50-plus-member Independent Games Festival (IGF) jury signed a statement declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, and urged the IGF to adopt a policy disallowing any AI-generated work.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Prestige awards gatekeepers are hardening against AI tools, raising reputational cost of AI use for indie studios.
insights.quote: declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity
insights.locator: This particular controversy has been brewing

insights.claim: IGF jurors reported a significant increase in submitted games developed with generative AI tools, and cited ecological, economic, psychological and labor harms.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Signals rising AI adoption in indie game development despite cultural backlash.

insights.claim: Some IGF jurors argue that even minimal AI use must be disqualifying as a deliberate cultural lever to steer the industry away from generative AI, regardless of the work's merit.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Anti-AI positioning in creative communities is political and absolutist, not proportional — expect continued boycotts.

insights.claim: House House said LLMs were used sparingly late in Big Walk's development, amounting to well under 0.1% of the code, to fix a Unity engine 'infinite length' shadow bug that a Unity engineer said was not fixable; the LLM suggestion was heavily modified into 10 lines of code.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Even last-resort, tiny AI use in code now carries disclosure and reputational risk for game studios.

insights.claim: Big Walk's Steam page received over 400 negative reviews after the disclosure, though Steam's anti-review-bomb tools limited the impact on its 'Very Positive' rating.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Platform review-bomb mitigation dampens commercial damage from AI controversies.
